source.title: Features Emerge as Discrete States: The First Application of SAEs to 3D Representations
source.authors: Albert J. Miao; Chen-Liang Zhou; Jia-Wei Zhou; C. Oztireli

page_placements.theme: Cross-seed and cross-size reproducibility of SAE features

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAEs to 3D representations and varies dictionary size, but it does not match features across dictionary sizes or test whether a smaller feature's inputs are partitioned among finer, nearby features.
record.gate_note: Appendix B.1 reports SAE universality at several codebook sizes and thresholds. Universality compares separately trained SAEs with the same hyperparameters; it does not compare features across dictionary sizes. The feature ablations and additions elsewhere in the paper do not test dictionary-size splitting.
record.test_reason: The study applies BatchTopK SAEs to Dora-VAE 3D latents. Its codebook-size variation (Appendix B.1) measures universality, the Procrustes-aligned cosine similarity between SAEs trained separately at the same size. It never matches features across sizes, never tests whether coarse features are covered by finer ones, and never examines hierarchy, absorption or the training objective. It mentions that 'more specific' features tile space differently only as a speculative explanation.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The main conclusion is that Dora-VAE features behave as discrete, state-like units with phase-like transitions under ablation. The authors explain this with a presence/identity learning-dynamics framework, and attribute the bimodal low-impact transition points to redistribution of superposition interference. The universality drop with codebook size is a minor appendix observation, with only a speculative explanation.
record.recipe_differences: BatchTopK SAEs trained on Dora-VAE pre-KL 3D latent activations; codebook-size and threshold variations, rather than a study of cross-size feature splitting.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported universality varies with codebook size; the table also varies threshold k.

fits_no_version.finding: Universality across separately trained SAEs falls from about 0.42 (n=256) to 0.29 (n=512) to 0.21 (n=1024), roughly independent of k. The authors speculate this reflects many possible tilings of positional features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In SAEs on a 3D VAE's latents, larger dictionaries yield less reproducible feature sets across training runs. This bears on SAE seed and data-split stability, not on cross-size splitting.

record.problems: The size-related universality metric compares independently trained SAEs at each setting, not features across sizes; no parent-child correspondence or shared-input partition is reported. The authors say code and encoded data will be available on release, without providing a release URL here.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were left out. The main-paper feature ablations and additions concern effects on 3D reconstructions, not dictionary-size splitting.

untested.parts: No cross-size feature matching, input-coverage test, or parent-child direction similarity.
No large-model or open-release SAEs, and no splitting analysis.
No feature families or concept hierarchy analysis.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and no count of novel latents.
No alternative objectives (e.g. Matryoshka) and no test of splitting as an objective artifact.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses call is correct. The phrase 'as features are allowed to become more specific' (B.1) is the only splitting-adjacent language, and it is untested speculation. Code is not yet released, and the paper is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: No cross-size feature matching, input-coverage partition test, or measurement of directions between parent and child features.
No large-model or open-SAE-release evaluation of splitting.
No test of nested feature families or whether they mirror a concept hierarchy.
No test of parent-child absorption or whether changing SAE size or sparsity fixes it.
No decomposition comparison between larger- and smaller-SAE latents or test for novel latents.
No test of whether splitting is an artifact of the sparsity objective or whether Matryoshka SAEs change it.

rows.problem: Table layout is flattened but the universality column is identifiable.

relation.reason: Reports a universality trend with codebook size and speculates larger dictionaries give more specific features, but does not test splitting.

tranche.reason: Codebook-size variation measures same-size universality only; no cross-size feature matching or splitting test.

source_check.notes: Universality is the middle column of Table 1; the text extraction flattened the table. Main-paper SAE is n=512, k=8; n=256 rows are Appendix B.1 variants. Authors speculate larger dictionaries give more specific features with varied tilings, untested.

statements.correction: Universality across 10 separately trained SAEs on Dora-VAE latents: n=256 0.420/0.421/0.420; n=512 0.293/0.297/0.295; n=1024 0.206/0.208/0.209 (k=4/8/16). Authors state features become less universal as codebook size grows.
